title: Add a guarded, agent-aware web search tool

questions.prompt: Which free search provider should be the default implementation?
questions.description: Both options avoid API keys. SearXNG gives JSON and metasearch quality but requires a self-hosted instance. DuckDuckGo Lite is fully zero-setup but needs light HTML scraping.

options.label: SearXNG (self-hosted, JSON API, no API key)
DuckDuckGo Lite (zero setup, HTML scraping)

questions.prompt: Should there be a built-in fallback when the primary provider fails?
questions.description: A fallback improves reliability but increases the code/testing surface.

options.label: Yes, fall back to DuckDuckGo Lite when SearXNG is unreachable
Yes, fall back to a secondary SearXNG base URL
No fallback — fail fast and return a clear error

questions.prompt: How deep should a search result go?
questions.description: The agent can ask for snippets only, or optionally fetch and strip the destination page. Deeper results are more useful but carry larger SSRF/active-content risks.

options.label: Return only title + snippet + URL from the search provider
Return snippets, and allow an optional :fetch? flag that fetches the page body
Always fetch and strip the first N result pages

questions.prompt: Which defensive guardrails must be shipped in the first version?
questions.description: Select the controls that are mandatory; unselected items can be future work.
questions.recommendedAnswer: All of: input/output Malli schemas; URL allow/deny lists with private-IP/localhost block; query length and special-char limits; result HTML stripping of scripts/iframes/forms; timeout and response-size caps; known injection-marker refusal; audit logging of every search and fetch; no recursive tool calls from search output.

options.label: Malli input/output schemas on tool and protocol
URL allow/deny lists (block localhost, private IPs, metadata endpoints)
Query length, encoding, and delimiter limits
Strip scripts, iframes, forms, and event handlers from fetched content
HTTP timeout and response-size caps
Refuse known prompt-injection markers in query and results
Audit-log every search and fetch
Prevent search output from triggering further tool calls
Human-in-the-loop for fetch mode
Secondary LLM guard that reviews every search call

questions.prompt: How should the provider be configured?
questions.description: E.g., EDN config key, runtime agent map key, or environment variable.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Via the agent EDN config under :tools/web-search with keys :provider, :base-url, :timeout-ms, :max-results, and optional :fetch? and :allow-hosts.

questions.description: Choose the minimum tests for the first version.
questions.recommendedAnswer: unit tests for schema validation, URL blocking, HTML stripping, and provider mocking; integration test with a local SearXNG container; adversarial tests for injection payloads.

options.label: Unit tests with mocked providers
Integration test against a local SearXNG Docker instance
Adversarial tests for prompt injection and SSRF payloads

questions.prompt: What should be explicitly out of scope?
questions.description: This protects the first version from scope creep.
questions.recommendedAnswer: No paid APIs (Brave/Bing/Google) in the default config; no LLM-based summarization of fetched pages; no browser/JS execution; no persistent caching of search results; no multi-step web browsing beyond a single optional fetch.

options.label: Paid search APIs as default providers
LLM summarization of fetched pages
Browser/JS execution (headless)
Persistent result cache
Multi-step browsing beyond one optional fetch
